capabilities: Read PDFs, EPUBs, saved web articles and YouTube transcripts inside Obsidian
Clip selected text or page regions into notes as quotes or PNG images
Nest clips under parent clips while reading
Track reading progress in a library of in-progress documents
Import a Readwise export as ordinary notes
disambiguation: Not a bulk PDF-to-Markdown converter; nothing enters the vault until you clip it yourself.
extras: Opt-in AI transcription is the only network feature and stays fully offline when the key is unset; the key is stored in Obsidian's secure storage and migrated from older plaintext versions. YouTube transcript saving and Apple Books import are desktop-only (the latter needs macOS Full Disk Access). MIT licensed with a Buy Me a Coffee link; the README documents a versioned public API for other plugins.
motivation: In the vault it was built for, 174 of 348 PDF page references in Excalidraw drawings were already broken because the named PDF no longer existed; the author decided a pointer is not storage, so clips become real files in the vault.
problem: Reading sources and taking quotes usually means external apps or bulk PDF-to-Markdown converters that dump a transcript into the vault, with no link between the highlight and the note you write about it.

relations.evidence: Import from a Readwise export turns the two files Readwise hands you on the way out
Send clips from this note to Excalidraw opens a gallery of every image clip

summary: Document reader for PDFs, EPUBs, web articles and video transcripts; clip passages as quotes or images and write your own text underneath.
